subject: Post-call recap: token volume bands, unit-econ targets, and signatory path
messages:
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
To: Anna Rivera <anna@brightlayer.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 12 Nov 2026 15:08:00 -0800
Subject: Post-call recap + next steps (token bands / who signs)

Hi Anna — thanks again for taking time today. Quick recap from our call and the asks I promised to follow up on: 

1) Volume bands you mentioned: pilot at ~200–400K tokens/month, expected ramp to 1M–1.5M tokens/mo in Q1 after model integration. You also flagged a potential stretch to ~3M tokens if embeddings usage expands.

2) Target unit economics: you said procurement has a target for line items to come in around $600–$1,200 per 1M tokens (depends on latency/throughput guarantees). For sizing we gave a back-of-envelope estimate — attaching an XLS with a few scenarios.

3) Approval path: you mentioned the product team owns technical signoff, and finance typically issues the PO / signs SOW for deals under $75k ARR, while larger commitments need VP Finance review. We want to be explicit on who will sign for each band.

Immediate next steps I propose:
- Anna / BrightLayer: confirm budget band you want us to price to for a pilot (e.g., 200–400K vs 1M target) and who will cut the PO for that band.
- Redwood: we’ll send a one-page cost estimate for 3 pricing points and a draft SOW (attached).

Would it help if I also loop in our finance lead to pre-seed the procurement language? If so, please confirm the name/email of your procurement contact (procure@brightlayer is fine if that’s the right inbox).

Thanks — I’ll follow up with the two files in the next email.

Best,
Evelyn Hart
Senior AE, Redwood Inference
Evelyn.Hart@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0142

Attachments: Redwood-1M-estimate.xlsx (spreadsheet), SOW-draft-v1.pdf (PDF)
From: Anna Rivera <anna@brightlayer.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
Cc: BrightLayer Procurement <procure@brightlayer.com>
Date: Fri, 13 Nov 2026 09:41:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-call recap + next steps (token bands / who signs)

Hi Evelyn — thanks for the summary and the files. Quick answers from our side: 

- Pilot band: we want the pilot priced at the 200–400K tokens/mo band. Target after integration is 1M tokens/mo, but we would like a two-tier price sheet that shows both pilot and 1M run-rate.
- Unit-econ target: Finance stated a preferred target around ~$900 per 1M tokens for this workload (we understand latency/throughput drives variance).
- Who signs: For the pilot ($Xk level) Procurement can issue the PO and will sign the SOW. Anything with a committed run-rate that projects >$100k ARR will need VP Finance (Amit Shah) sign-off.

Procurement contact is the shared inbox (procure@brightlayer.com); I copied them so they have context.

Next: please send the 3-point estimate and a pilot SOW with cancellation / scale clauses.

Anna
Anna Rivera
Head of AI Integrations, BrightLayer
anna@brightlayer.com

On Thu, Nov 12, 2026 at 3:08 PM Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai> wrote:
> (call recap)
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 14 Nov 2026 08:12:00 -0800
Subject: Fwd: Post-call recap + next steps (token bands / who signs) — procurement path clarified by Anna

Karthik / Markus — forwarding BrightLayer’s reply so we’re aligned on approval cadence. Key points: pilot = 200–400K/mo priced to ~$900/1M target (they expect ~ $900 but accept variance). Procurement (procure@brightlayer.com) will issue PO for pilot; VP Finance (Amit Shah) signs anything > $100k ARR.

Questions for pricing:
- Do we build a 3-line price sheet with explicit PO thresholds (pilot / 1M / 3M) and a short note that discounts apply for committed volumes?
- For commercial: do we recommend adding a 60-day exit / trial clause in the pilot SOW to reduce friction?

I sketched three candidate price points in the XLS attached to the original mail. If we standardize the PO thresholds we can speed up procurement.

If Markus agrees I’ll prepare a single-page pricing matrix + pilot SOW and loop in Finance (Markus suggested he can introduce our finance contact directly to theirs).

—Evelyn

P.S. I think keeping the pilot under procurement-only signoff is the fast path; we avoid VP review unless they opt into a run-rate commitment sooner.
From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 15 Nov 2026 10:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Fwd: Post-call recap + next steps (token bands / who signs) — procurement path clarified by Anna

Thanks — good summary. Two quick asks before we send anything to procurement: 

1) Evelyn: please include a clear low-touch PO option for the pilot that does not enumerate long-term commitments (60-day trial language is fine). Call out an explicit pilot cancellation window and an easy upgrade path.
2) Karthik / Finance ops: please confirm the recommended $/1M token list price tiers for pilot vs committed run-rate and flags for SLA tiers (e.g., standard vs low-latency). If we can keep the pilot at a single list price and present discounts for 1M/3M committed bands, procurement can approve faster.

Once we have the single-page matrix I’ll make the intros to Amit Shah and request a short procurement meeting to agree PO language.

Markus Klein
Head of Sales Operations, Redwood Inference
markus.klein@redwood.ai
